# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-row mapping: first mark to red, second to blue, third to green. I am sending Deaf a structured visual relay: row numbers followed by color tokens, using stop for red, a distinct sign for blue, and go for green. Deaf can then describe the observed engraving and tell Blind which wire color to cut.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✋", "✌", "🤙", "🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The plate has one engraved mark that I can feel but cannot identify or pronounce. I have no reliable information about the display, light, or wires. Please consult the manual for the plate rule and have Deaf report the visible bomb details before giving me any cut instruction.

The manual requires identifying the engraved mark and mapping it to a wire color. Since Deaf can see the mark and can speak to Blind, I am sending a compact visual code: the three entries are in table order, with one, two, and three raised-finger signals representing red, blue, and green respectively. Deaf should identify which table entry matches the engraving, then tell Blind the corresponding color.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please translate the gesture sequence into the manual's explicit instruction: which wire position should I cut for display 0, light off, question-mark plate, and wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green?

The plate’s display and light are irrelevant under this manual. The only needed fact is which of the three engraved marks is present; its table row directly gives the matching wire position here: row 1 → wire 1 (red), row 2 → wire 2 (blue), row 3 → wire 3 (green). I am giving Deaf that mapping and asking Deaf to inspect the mark and verbally tell Blind the corresponding wire position.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "👋", "✌", "✌", "👋", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gestures. Please send the decoded wire position as spoken words or a number, not gestures.

I cannot send spoken words or numbers, and Blind cannot see my gestures. Deaf must therefore inspect the engraved mark and relay the resulting wire position aloud. The three signals below establish the manual’s row order—one, two, three—so Deaf can match the visible mark to the corresponding wire position and tell Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send exactly one gesture to Deaf to identify the wire to cut: index finger up means wire 1, victory sign means wire 2, love-you hand means wire 3. Do not send any other gestures.

I do not know which engraved mark Deaf sees, so choosing any one of the three gestures would be an unsupported wire instruction and could detonate the bomb. I cannot safely send exactly one identifying gesture without Deaf first reporting the mark.

```

```

The manual only defines three engraved marks: ꕥ, ꖜ, and ꗃ. Deaf reports a question mark, which does not match any defined mark, so no wire can be determined safely. I must not guess among the three required gestures.
